headline: US chip stocks fell for an eighth straight session on Friday, their longest losing run since 2008.
score_reason: Record-length chip sell-off confirmed by several outlets; it extends a story already carried, so the score is kept but not raised.
importance_line: Holders of chip-heavy funds are hit first, then chip makers and their suppliers, but the semiconductor index is still up about 57% this year per Reuters, so this may be a sharp pullback rather than proof that the AI boom is over.
source: Capital Brief, citing Bloomberg and Reuters
summary: Capital Brief, relaying Bloomberg and Reuters reporting, says US chip stocks fell for an eighth straight session on Friday, their longest losing run since 2008, with the main semiconductor index down 3.8% and Broadcom down 4.5%. This continues our 16 Oct coverage, when Business Insider reported chip stocks caught in a $1 trillion wipeout; new today is the eighth straight loss, while investors moved into energy and utilities shares, which rose 2.5% and 1.4%.
notes: The Edge Singapore original is blocked (403); text read at Capital Brief, which credits Bloomberg, Reuters and WSJ, so the source is given as Capital Brief citing Bloomberg and Reuters. The 57% year-to-date semiconductor figure is from Reuters Week Ahead (C07-03).
